sentences: Preheat the oven to 190C/170C Fan/Gas 5 and grease a 26cm/10in spring-from cake tin.

Preheat the oven to 180C/160C Fan/Gas 4.
Grease a 20cm/8in square cake tin with butter, then line the base and sides with baking paper.
Use a tablespoon or so of the sauce to coat the turkey, then place this on top.

Put the chicken in a bowl with one tablespoon each of the soy sauce, Shaoxing rice wine and sesame oil.
Add one tablespoon of the vegetable oil, and when it is hot and slightly smoking, add the chicken and stir fry for 2-3 minutes, or until nearly cooked through.
Add the remaining two tablespoons of Shaoxing rice wine, one tablespoon of the soy, all the sugar and chicken stock and bring to the boil.
Finish with a third of the spring onion and a tablespoon of coriander and stir through.
Set aside and heat another wok until hot, add one tablespoon of vegetable oil, half the remaining ginger, garlic and chilli mix and half the remaining spring onion and stir fry for one minute.
Add the bok choi and 75ml/3fl oz of water and stir fry until the bok choi is tender and the liquid evaporated.
Add one tablespoon of coriander and half the remaining spring onion and stir fry for one minute then put onto the serving plate.
For the chicken nuggets, heat the oil in a deep-fat fryer to 180C/350F.
Preheat the oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4 and line a 30x20cm/12x8in tin with baking parchment.
Add the trout and poach gently at 50C for 10–15 minutes, take the fish to 48 degrees and allow to rest for at least 5 minutes before serving.
To make the crisp Belgian endive, whisk 50ml/2fl oz reserved poaching oil with the sweet muscatel vinegar, crème fraîche and mustard to make a dressing.

To make the flatbreads, pour 300ml/½ pint of warm water into a large mixing bowl, then sprinkle in the yeast and sugar.
Pour about 1 tablespoon of olive oil into a medium-sized bowl and rub it in with your hands.
Tear off handfuls of dough about the size of a tangerine, or 100g/3½oz. Take one and flatten it with your hands to create a vaguely circular shape about 2mm/1/16in thick.
Add 1 teaspoon of salt and give it a good mix, then leave to sit for a bit.
Add a pinch of salt and massage in with your hands for a few minutes to soften the cabbage.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok and fry the chillies, peppercorns and celery for 2–3 minutes, then remove from the pan and drain on kitchen paper.
Heat 2 teaspoons of the oil in a large, non-stick frying pan over a medium heat.
Add the chopped tomatoes, chipotle paste, beans and 600ml/20fl oz cold water to the saucepan.
